family: Amendments of the Civil Service Rules and related class orders (X1 type cs_rules_amendment), 1872-1936

mechanisms.description: An order whose own operative text only amends the Civil Service Rules, a schedule, another order or a presidential regulation has no command of its own after issue: its text merges into the parent and lives or ends with the parent (coordinator ruling P2). Later orders that amend the text it inserted are events of the parent.
An order whose only operative content revokes or rescinds another order is spent on issue (ruling P1).

EO 89 (May 6, 1896) 'makes and promulgates the following rules and revokes all others': an express revocation of a described class, every civil service rule the President had made, which reaches each rule set, extension and rule-making order made before that day.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: 1896-05-06, approval date of EO 89 (the member may have ended earlier)

mechanisms.description: EO 209 promulgates its rules 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof': an express description of the instrument it displaces, the rules of May 6, 1896 (EO 89).

EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01, and EO 9830 (1947) and EO 10577 (1955) restated them again. A whole-text restatement 'to read as follows' that does not name an order does not end it (ruling P3); the 1939 restatement is recorded as a disclosed earlier candidate end for EO 209.
A later order that names the member, by number or by its date, revoked, rescinded or superseded it as a whole.

The present Civil Service Rules (5 CFR parts 1-10, from EO 10577 as amended) and excepted-position schedules (5 CFR part 213, OPM regulations) carry forward the subject matter of the old rules under later instruments; they neither end nor show in force any 1872-1936 member.

procedure.description: One-person orders typed into this family: one act for one or two named persons (appointment without examination, classification with a position, re-certification, rating of one candidate's papers, retention, designation).

lead.basis: The order's operative content is one act for a named person, so it belongs to the one-person civil service family PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (ruling P4), whose evidence-of-use and life-of-person rules decide it.

gaps: apply PD-CS-ONE-PERSON; EO 3050 (Robert L. Stancill, February 1919) and EO 3051 (Bert M. Williams, 1919) are readable one-person appointment waivers in ProQuest scans; EO 3425 amends EO 3398 only to accord a classified status to Henry F. Brown; EO 691 names two persons

procedure.description: Special rules of 1897-1902 promulgated as freestanding rules (not amendments of a numbered rule).

lead.basis: A special rule is a freestanding rule. EO 209 replaced the 1896 rules 'and the amendments thereof', but EO 250 revoked a 1902 special rule in 1904, which shows special rules were treated as outlasting the 1903 revision; whether and when each ended is not established.

gaps: for each special rule: its own terms and any later revocation (Civil Service Commission reports FY1897-FY1905). EO 97 and EO 98 except only 'the successor to the present incumbent' and were probably exhausted by one appointment (no record of it is held). EO 191 lets the engineer of the new Government Printing Office building retain his force 'during the continuance of the work at the War College and Washington Barracks', and 'The authority herein granted shall lapse upon the completion of said work': an own-terms (TERM) end that needs only the completion date of that work

procedure.description: Classification orders under section 6 of the Civil Service Act (heads directed to amend their classifications), even where the WPA calls them rule amendments.

lead.basis: The order directs department heads to classify a group of positions under section 6 of the 1883 Act; its effect (positions classified) is a continuing state, and no held instrument is shown to have ended it. Later rules saved status so granted (EO 7915 Rule II sec. 1), which is not an end.

gaps: per-position evidence: for the positions named (State Department messengers and watchmen, departmental firemen, pension agency employees), a later order or statute that names them and excepts them, abolishes them or reorganizes their office; or the Civil Service Commission annual report that records their removal from the classified service

procedure.description: Rule sets prescribed, extended or approved before the 1896 revision (Grant-era rules of 1872-1874; Internal Revenue and Government Printing Office rules of 1895).

lead.basis: EO 89 (May 6, 1896) 'makes and promulgates the following rules and revokes all others'. The words expressly revoke a described class, every other civil service rule; the member is in that class because its own text shows it prescribes, extends or approves civil service rules under R.S. 1753, the power EO 89 recites.

date_rule.basis: EO 89 approved May 6, 1896; the member may have ended earlier (the Grant-era rules lapsed in practice after 1875; not relied on)

gaps: member test: the member is dated before May 6, 1896 and its own text (or, for a scan, its WPA summary) shows it prescribes, extends, approves or amends civil service rules the President made under R.S. 1753 and the 1883 Act, the authority EO 89 itself recites

EO 15's text is an unread scan and its class membership rests on its WPA summary ('Regulations governing classification of the Civil Service, prescribed Apr. 16, 1872, amended'); EO 17's scan is readable only in its closing lines ('extended to the several Federal offices at the city and in the customs district of B[o]ston')
EO 89 is held as Richardson's printed compilation, not the signed original

procedure.description: Pure revocations of another order or special rule.

lead.basis: The member's own text only revokes or rescinds another order ('hereby revoked' / 'hereby rescinded'); it is spent on issue as a command, and its effect is evidence for the revoked order's lifecycle (ruling P1).

procedure.description: Waivers, suspensions or exemptions of the rules (not amendments of their text).

lead.basis: The order waives or suspends a rule for a person, group or occasion rather than changing the rule's text. Waivers for named persons belong to PD-CS-ONE-PERSON; class and occasion waivers (EO 713 carriage drivers, EO 1275 furloughed Lighthouse Service employees, EO 7366 initial Social Security Board appointments) have no family doctrine yet.

gaps: apply PD-CS-ONE-PERSON to named-person waivers; for class waivers, the order's own terms (occasion, period, positions) and evidence of use

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

lead.basis: The order places a group of positions (often with their incumbents) in or out of the classified service, or excepts them, without amending the rules' text. Its effect is a continuing state of coverage; no held instrument names it, the later restatements do not end it (ruling P3), and EO 7915 Rule II sec. 1 saved status granted 'by executive orders covering groups of employees with their positions into the competitive classified service', which is a savings clause, not an end.

gaps: per-position evidence that would decide a member: (1) a later executive order or statute that names this order or the positions it covers and excepts them, abolishes them, or transfers them to a statutory personnel system; (2) a Civil Service Commission annual report or Federal Register notice recording the removal of the positions from Schedule A/B or from the classified service; (3) abolition of the office or bureau holding the positions by a statute or reorganization plan with a stated date; (4) for orders placing positions outside the classified service (EO 1394, 6772, 6784), the end of the commission or office concerned
the branch also catches a few loosely matched orders of other kinds (EO 633, 91, 984, 178, 416), open either way

procedure.description: Separate presidential regulation sets prescribed, extended or approved (labor, postmaster, efficiency rating, furlough).

gaps: the later order that names and replaces each regulation set (postmaster regulations of 1917, 1926, 1929 and 1936; labor regulations of 1904-1909) and its revocation clause
